To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the GALEX FUV counts are in agreement with previous GALEX studies, but (2) the NUV counts are higher than previous studies, and (3) the GALEx FUV-NUV color distribution of galaxies in our field is bimodal, with one population of blue galaxies (NUV-FUV < 1) and a population of red galaxies (NUV - FUV > 2.5).

we have measured a similar to 2 mag deeper source catalog in the UV than previously reported for the Coma cluster and that we have measured UV galaxy counts that agree with the deeper counts measured with HST.

the GALEx source detection algorithm is limited in sensitivity by source confusion, and that our source catalog is complete and reliable for galaxies with NUV < 23.0 and FUV < 23, and is useful for studying the UV properties of galaxies out to NUV similar to24.5 and similar to FUV similar to25.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the UV properties of galaxies in the Coma cluster.
the study of the faintest UV sources in Coma and the impact that these sources have on UV number counts.
the UV properties of galaxies in a nearby rich cluster and the UV background light in the local universe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we find that the GALEXX counts in Coma are consistent with the HST counts, but not with GALEX counts in other regions.

the UV counts from this work, which are based on a deep, well-calibrated UV image and a robust cataloging method, provide the best match to the UV counts from the Hubble Space Telescope and are consistent with the predictions of the semi-empirical galaxy formation model of Somerville et al. (2001).
the GALEx pipeline counts are consistent with the deeper HST counts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our GALEX catalog is the most complete to date for a deep UV survey of a cluster of galaxies.
the GALEx FUV and NUV counts are in good agreement with previous studies at NUV = 20-21, but are significantly higher at NUV < 21.

our GALEX observations are deep enough that the UV field galaxy number counts are not yet well understood, but our catalog is sufficiently complete that it can be used to study UV properties of individual galaxies in the cluster and the surrounding field.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the GALEXX catalog of the Coma field is deep enough to detect a significant number of resolved galaxies, and that the GALEXXX pipeline catalog is confusion limited for NUV similar to FUV similar to23.
the Coma cluster field has a very high density of UV-bright galaxies, and this is reflected in the GALEX counts.
GALEX is an extremely valuable instrument for measuring the UV properties of galaxies, especially in the case of deep fields where the GALEX source catalogs are confusion limited.
